entities.name: The Silmarillion
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Silmarillion is a collection of myths and stories written by J.R. Tolkien, detailing the history of Middle-earth from its creation to the end of the First Age.

Written in the early 20th century, The Silmarillion drew heavily from Norse and Celtic mythologies, as well as Christian theology, to create a unique narrative that explores the intersection of mortal and divine realms.

The book's significance lies in its influence on modern fantasy literature, with many authors citing Tolkien as a major inspiration. The Silmarillion has also been recognized for its cultural importance, featuring in various exhibitions and publications celebrating the works of J.R. Tolkien.

In 2019, The Silmarillion was adapted into an animated film by Amazon Studios, marking a new era of interest in the book's narrative. This adaptation has sparked renewed discussion about the book's themes and characters, introducing them to a wider audience.

This entity matters historically because it represents one of the earliest attempts to create a comprehensive mythology for Middle-earth, setting the stage for the development of modern fantasy literature.
